solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Stupid rat getting caught for good

indicators.note: one thing getting another in place of something signals a swap of letters
X for Y means X stands where Y used to be in the word

parts.note: to rat on someone is to grass, inform on them
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
G is the standard abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A rodent is caught and somehow its stupidity is gone for good.
explanation.walkthrough: In GRASS the G (good) is replaced by C (caught), giving CRASS. To grass is British slang for informing to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Crass describes behaviour that is grossly insensitive or dim-witted, a close synonym of stupid.

clue.text: Parrot picking out article from treetops

indicators.note: picking something out removes it, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: the canopy is the upper layer of a forest
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A bird picks out something from high in the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: Parrot looks like the bird doing the picking, but it is a verb meaning mimic. CANOPY loses AN.
explanation.definitionFit: To parrot words is to repeat them mechanically, that is, to imitate or copy them.

clue.text: Plants reptiles around one officer's craft going north

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so this word wraps the following pieces

parts.note: asps are snakes
I is the Roman numeral one
DI is a Detective Inspector, with the possessive S

indicators.note: in a down clue going north means reading upward, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: art means skill or craft

explanation.surface: Botanical reptiles surround a detective's vehicle heading up the country.
explanation.walkthrough: Craft suggests a boat, but it means skill. A DI is a Detective Inspector in British police ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: Aspidistras are leafy, hardy houseplants, so they are plants.

clue.text: Better half of swamp drained at head of river

indicators.note: at the head of means placed in front of the next piece
drained means emptied, so the middle is removed and only the outer letters stay

parts.note: the outside letters of swamp
the Ouse is a river in England

explanation.surface: The better part of a marsh is drained near a river's source.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ouse is the name of several English rivers, including the one through York.
explanation.definitionFit: Better half is a jocular idiom for one's husband or wife, so it means a spouse.

clue.text: Appreciate artist visiting ruins for day of celebration

indicators.note: someone visiting a place goes inside it, so these words sit within the other piece

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or ruin; mars is the third-person form
to dig something is slang for appreciating it
RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys an artist turning up among ruins on a festive day.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruins is a verb here, not the noun for crumbling buildings the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Mardi Gras, Shrove Tuesday, is the carnival day of feasting before Lent begins.

clue.text: Sweet infused with eastern mace cracked baker's filling

indicators.note: a liquid infused with something has it steeped inside, so pieces go within

parts.note: a mint is a sweet

indicators.note: something cracked is broken apart, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dessert flavoured with oriental spice that was ground up for a pie.
explanation.walkthrough: Mincemeat in Britain is a sweet fruit mix, usually with no meat at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Mincemeat is the spiced fruit mixture bakers put inside mince pies, so it is a pastry filling.

clue.text: Test edges of rare stone one's cutting

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its outermost letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of rare

indicators.note: something cutting into another goes inside it

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for a stone in weight
I is the Roman numeral one; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: Checking the rims of a rare gem with something cutting it.
explanation.walkthrough: Stone is the British weight unit of 14 pounds, not a gem; the 's in one's stands for is.
explanation.definitionFit: A resit is an exam taken again after failing, so it is a test.

clue.text: Clumsy fiancée occasionally cross and cheeky

indicators.note: occasionally means every now and then, so only every other letter is kept

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters
an X is a cross
pert means saucy or cheeky

explanation.surface: A clumsy fiancée is sometimes angry and impudent.
explanation.walkthrough: Cross looks like the adjective angry, but it gives the letter X.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone inexpert lacks skill, so their handling of a task is awkward or clumsy.

clue.text: Standard that's been raised in music

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means lifted upward, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: par is the standard or norm

explanation.surface: A standard that has been raised in the music world.
explanation.definitionFit: Rap is a genre of music with rhythmic spoken lyrics, so it is music in the sense of a style.

clue.text: Grabs second tour running in European city

indicators.note: running suggests motion and flux, so these letters are set moving into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for second
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone snatches a second tour of a city on the run.
explanation.definitionFit: Strasbourg is a city in north-eastern France and seat of the European Parliament.

clue.text: Sorry knight taking copper contents of bucket?

indicators.note: a word taking something in holds it inside itself

parts.note: sorry as in a sorry state: poor, pitiful
a copper is a police officer, a PC (police constable)
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A wretched knight takes the copper out of a bucket.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the bucket is a cinema snack tub, not a pail.
explanation.definitionFit: At the cinema popcorn is commonly sold in a large bucket, so it is what fills one.

clue.text: Small shelter for every part of track

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
per means for each, as in miles per hour

explanation.surface: A little shelter is provided for every section of a route.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a sleeper is the timber or concrete beam the railway lines rest on (a tie in the US).
explanation.definitionFit: Sleepers are the cross-beams laid under the rails, so each one is a component of railway track.

clue.text: Spy anxious about scooping items?

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the two words are read from the far end back

parts.note: a snoop is someone who spies or pries
anxious means stressed

explanation.surface: A nervous secret agent fretting about something, perhaps an ice-cream scoop.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words are read backwards as one string; the well-known stressed/desserts pairing does most of the work.
explanation.definitionFit: Dessert spoons are the mid-sized spoons used to scoop up puddings, so they are implements for scooping.

clue.text: Old maiden brought up popular gift that's everywhere

parts.note: O is the abbreviation for old
M is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: brought up in a down clue means carried upward, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
a present is a gift

explanation.surface: An old maiden lady was raised with a popular gift.
explanation.walkthrough: IN turns to NI. A maiden is a cricket over with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Omnipresent means present in all places at once, which is the sense of being everywhere.

clue.text: Chap traversing tops of wild areas lugging kit?

definitions.text: Chap traversing tops of wild areas lugging kit?

indicators.note: to traverse something is to go across it, so this word spans the other piece

parts.note: feller is an informal word for a chap

indicators.note: the tops of words are their first letters

parts.note: the first letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A man carrying gear across the high ground of the wilds.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer. Fells are the hills of northern England, such as the Lake District.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellwalker hikes across hills and moorland carrying a rucksack, exactly the person the clue pictures.

clue.text: Nauseous queen taking leave of child's play

indicators.note: taking leave means departing, so those letters go away from the word

parts.note: feeling nauseous is feeling sick or queasy
QU is a standard abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: A queen feels sick as she leaves a children's game.
explanation.walkthrough: QUEASY loses QU.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is child's play is so simple a child could do it, which is to say effortless.

clue.text: Person ate cooked tongue

indicators.note: cooked figuratively means altered or falsified, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone dined on cooked ox tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: Tongue looks like the food that was cooked, but it means a language.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is an invented international language, and tongue is a common word for a language.

clue.text: Advanced intelligence of spin over large net-zero town?

indicators.note: over in a down clue means placed above, so this piece comes first

parts.note: spin is public relations, PR
an eco-city is a planned city designed to be carbon-neutral; a city is a large town

explanation.surface: A clever bit of publicity for a town with green credentials.
explanation.definitionFit: Precocity is development ahead of one's age, especially a child's unusually advanced mental ability.

clue.text: In conclusion, some papers sought information

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

parts.note: the end is the conclusion
a quire is a set of 24 or 25 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: In the end, a few newspapers made inquiries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In conclusion' reads as a phrase meaning finally, but in is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To enquire is to ask questions, so enquired is the past tense meaning asked for facts.

clue.text: Short message involving gold frame of green specs

definitions.note: plural, but a lorgnette is a single pair of spectacles

indicators.note: to involve something is to wrap it up inside, so other pieces go within
a short version of a word has its final letter cut off

parts.note: a letter is a written message
or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: a frame is the outer border, so only the outside letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of green

explanation.surface: A brief note mentions gold-framed green-tinted glasses.
explanation.walkthrough: Gold as or comes from heraldry, where it is the word for that colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorgnette is a pair of glasses held up to the eyes on a long handle, an old-fashioned kind of spectacles.

clue.text: Box spring beginning to rust

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: the first letter of rust

explanation.surface: A box spring, the base of a bed, starting to go rusty.
explanation.walkthrough: Box spring reads as one bed-base item, but box is the definition and spring is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To box and to spar both mean to fight with the fists, especially in practice.

clue.text: Picture husband abandoning inexperienced firm

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so that letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: fresh as in new to something, green
H is the abbreviation for husband
CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: An image of a husband walking out on a new business.
explanation.walkthrough: FRESH loses H, and CO is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A fresco is a painting done on wet plaster on a wall or ceiling, a kind of picture.

clue.text: Series of obstacles in report of a sailor's training?

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so we go by how the words are spoken

parts.note: a salt is an old sailor, and a course is a period of training

explanation.surface: A list of hurdles appears in an account of naval training.
explanation.walkthrough: A salt (old salt) is a seasoned sailor; said aloud, a salt's course matches the obstacle course's name.
explanation.definitionFit: An assault course is a military training circuit of walls, nets and ditches to clamber over: a run of obstacles.

clue.text: Claw sample of phenolates back

indicators.note: back means going in the backward direction, so read from right to left
a sample is a small portion taken from something larger

parts.note: letters inside the word, from its middle

explanation.surface: A chemist takes a sample of a claw back to analyse its phenolates.
explanation.walkthrough: Phenolates are salts of phenol; the word is chosen only for the letters it holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is the hooked claw of a bird of prey.

clue.text: Stay with last of climbers on summit

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of climbers
the top is the summit

explanation.surface: Remain on the peak alongside the last of the mountaineers.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay somewhere is to stop there, as in stopping overnight at a hotel.

clue.text: Bird right by street bisecting part of Hull

indicators.note: bisecting means cutting in two, so these letters split the other word in the middle

parts.note: the keel is part of a ship's hull
ST is the abbreviation for street
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A bird of prey spotted by a road running through part of the city of Hull.
explanation.walkthrough: Hull is capitalised to suggest the Yorkshire city, but it is a ship's hull.
explanation.definitionFit: The kestrel is a small falcon known for hovering, so it is a bird.

clue.text: Relatives rejecting third appeal for help

indicators.note: rejecting the third means throwing out the third letter in line

parts.note: sons are relatives

explanation.surface: Family members spurn a third plea for assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: SONS loses its third letter, N.
explanation.definitionFit: SOS is the Morse distress signal, a standard call for rescue.

clue.text: Check out six-footer nursing Penny

indicators.note: nursing something means holding it close, so one piece is cradled inside the other

parts.note: insects have six legs, so six feet
P is the abbreviation for penny

explanation.surface: Take a look at a very tall person holding a coin.
explanation.walkthrough: Six-footer suggests a tall person; it is a creature with six feet. P goes inside INSECT.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect something is to examine it closely, the same as checking it out.

clue.text: DIY screen ruined run of regular gigs

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A home-made stage screen spoiled a band's series of shows.
explanation.definitionFit: A residency is a period in which a performer plays repeatedly at the same venue.

clue.text: Senior citizen keeping books readily available

indicators.note: keeping something means holding on to it, so one piece is held within the other

parts.note: OAP is old-age pensioner, the British term for a senior citizen
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: An elderly person keeps a stock of books close at hand.
explanation.walkthrough: Books are biblical books here, as in the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer on tap flows whenever wanted, so the idiom means available whenever needed.
